To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

after 7 year of continuous cultivation of genetically modified (GM) Bt corn, total soil C and soil C mineralizable during 35-day incubations were not significantly different between the GM and non-GM treatments.
, after 6 years of continuous cropping, soil C and N were not significantly different between Bts and non-Bts corn.
seven years of continuously planted genetically modified Bt corn did neither affect total soil C and soil N nor the amount of C mineralized during an incubation period of 35 days.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of continuous cultivation of genetically modified Bt corn on soil characteristics.
the effects of genetically modified crops on soil C and N pools.
the long-term effects of genetically engineered Bt corn on the soil C and N pools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
after 7 year of continuous Bt corn, soil C and N levels were not affected by Bt corn.

after 7 year of continuous cultivation of a Bt corn variety, there were no detectable differences in soil total C and N levels and in soil C mineralized in surface soil between Bt and a non-Bt corn treatment.
after 7 year of continuous Bt corn cultivation, no significant changes in soil total C, total nitrogen and C mineralized during an incubation period were observed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of Cry endotoxins in the soil did not affect the mineralization rate or the amount of total soil C and soil N in surface soil after seven years of Bt corn cultivation.
Bt corn does not have any significant impact on soil C or N after 7 year of continuous cropping, at least in this study.
, at the scale of our study, the presence of Bt corn residues in the soil does not have a significant effect on soil C and N dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of Bt corn on soil C and N are likely to be small, and that the differences between Bt and conventional corn in the long term are likely to be smaller than those reported for the short term.
, after 6 years of continuous Bt corn cultivation, there is no indication of a change in the amount of soil C and N in surface soil.
the differences in soil properties between Bt and conventional corn treatments were not statistically detectable after 7 year of Bt corn cultivation.
